source_citation: Shaffer F, Ginsberg JP. An Overview of Heart Rate Variability Metrics and Norms. Front Public Health. 2017;5:258.
claim_summary: RMSSD (vagally-mediated HRV) decrease indicates a shift toward higher autonomic arousal.
known_limitations: Confounded by respiration rate, physical motion, posture, and caffeine; RMSSD is highly individual so absolute thresholds do not transfer between people.
extracted_excerpt: RMSSD reflects vagally mediated changes in HRV; reductions accompany sympathetic activation and reduced parasympathetic tone.

source_citation: Kim H-G, et al. Stress and Heart Rate Variability: A Meta-Analysis. Psychiatry Investig. 2018;15(3):235-245.
claim_summary: Reduced high-frequency HRV power reflects sympathetic dominance consistent with stress/arousal.
known_limitations: HF-HRV is strongly modulated by respiration rate and posture; short-window estimates are noisy; effect sizes vary widely across stress paradigms.
extracted_excerpt: Across studies, acute stress was associated with decreased HF-HRV power, indicating reduced parasympathetic activity.

source_citation: Kim H-G, et al. Stress and Heart Rate Variability: A Meta-Analysis. Psychiatry Investig. 2018;15(3):235-245.
claim_summary: Sustained elevated heart rate (outside exercise) indicates increased arousal.
known_limitations: Strong exercise/physical-exertion confound; must be gated to a non-exercise sub-context. Also raised by caffeine, fever, dehydration, and medication.
extracted_excerpt: Tonic heart-rate elevation co-occurs with sympathetic arousal when metabolic demand is controlled for.

source_citation: Lin CT, et al. EEG-Based Assessment of Cognitive Workload: Theta/Beta Ratio. (representative cognitive-load EEG literature).
claim_summary: Elevated frontal-midline theta/beta ratio indicates higher cognitive load.
known_limitations: Highly electrode-placement sensitive; contaminated by ocular/muscle artifacts; theta/beta also tracks drowsiness, so it must be disambiguated from low-arousal states.
extracted_excerpt: Frontal-midline theta increases and beta changes yield a rising theta/beta ratio under increasing working-memory demand.

source_citation: Coan JA, Allen JJB. Frontal EEG asymmetry as a moderator and mediator of emotion. Biol Psychol. 2004;67(1-2):7-49.
claim_summary: Relatively greater right-than-left frontal alpha (right>left) is associated with withdrawal/negative affect.
known_limitations: Contested literature with poor test-retest reliability; reference-montage dependent; trait vs state confound. Treat as a very weak prior; do not act on it alone.
extracted_excerpt: Greater relative right frontal activity (right>left alpha asymmetry) has been linked to withdrawal-related negative affect, though findings are inconsistent.

source_citation: Juslin PN, Scherer KR. Vocal expression of affect. In: The New Handbook of Methods in Nonverbal Behavior Research. 2005.
claim_summary: Faster speech rate and higher high-frequency vocal energy accompany increased arousal.
known_limitations: Heavy language, dialect, and individual-baseline variation; microphone and distance dependent; speech rate also rises with task urgency independent of affect.
extracted_excerpt: High-arousal affective states are reliably marked by increased speech rate and elevated high-frequency spectral energy.
